**Motif:** This is a **fork**—the knight on g6 attacks both the queen and the rook, forcing Black into a losing sequence.

**Coaching note (80 words max):**

Your queen on f6 was perfectly placed to attack a knight. When you captured it with Nxg6, you created a fork: your knight attacked both the queen (undefended) and the rook. Black had to give up the queen to avoid losing it outright. Always scan for your pieces creating two threats at once—knights especially love to fork the queen and a nearby piece. This position shows how a strong queen placement sets up the winning tactic.
